'''Uru''' was a [[Planet/Legends|world]]<ref name="MS" /> located within the [[Atravis sector/Legends|Atravis sector]] of<ref name="EAOC" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="MS" /><ref name="EAOC" /> An [[Alien/Legends|alien]] [[Species/Legends|species]]<ref name="CE" /> [[Oni]] was hailed from Uru.<ref name="MS" /><ref name="CE" /> The Oni people shared a bellicose<ref name="MS" /> culture<ref name="CE" /> and, by the time of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]],<ref name="MS" /> they were often found offworld as part of [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] [[Army/Legends|armies]].<ref name="CE" />

==Behind the scenes==
Uru was first mentioned in [[2004]] novel ''[[MedStar II: Jedi Healer]]'', co-authored by [[Michael Reaves]] and [[Steve Perry]].<ref name="MS" /> Later, the [[2009]] sourcebook ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', placed the [[Uru system/Legends|Uru star system]] in grid square L-19.<ref name="EAOC" />

According to [[Joseph Bongiorno]], the Oni species was intended by [[MedStar II: Jedi Healer]] as a reference to the Oni species of Oniboshi in the Japanese anime and manga series [[Wikipedia:Urusei_Yatsura|''Urusei Yatsura'']] by [[Wikipedia:Rumiko_Takahashi|Rumiko Takahashi]]. As both species are militant, both species' females are shown to be capable of generating electricity, and the [[Star Wars]] Oni come from Uru as in Urusei, this would indeed seem to be likely.<ref name="timelines" >{{WebCite|url=https://www.starwarstimeline.net/Supernatural_Encounters.htm|text=I heard there are a lot of crossovers. What is that about?|work=www.starwarstimeline.net|quote=in MedStar II: Jedi Healer, Michael Reaves and Steve Perry reference the Oni of Uru, which come from the 1980s anime-manga series, Urusei Yatsura, which itself referenced Star Wars.|archivedate=20250211153149}}</ref>
